title: [D4 Agents] Model client, structured output and bounded schema retry
summary: helena.agents is a working model client: ModelClient.for_agent(settings, agent) resolves one agent's endpoint, token and model purely from configuration, and assess(request, client=, messages=, policy=) calls the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, validates the answer against the frozen helena.contracts.v1.AgentResult, retries a bounded number of times with the validation error fed back, and turns exhaustion into a typed AgentFailure. It ran against the real configured endpoint in the suite and validated on the first attempt. No runtime dependency was added: LangChain is NOT here, because langchain-openai pulls langsmith and hosted tracing is rejected rather than deferred, and that conflict is escalated rather than resolved by a session.
assumption_validated: That an agent can be given the frozen contract as its output schema and answer it, without a framework and without a second schema. Confirmed against the configured endpoint on 2026-09-07, and it took two corrections that inspection would not have found: (1) the contract's closed vocabularies live in model_post_init, so model_json_schema() reports a bare string for Citation.stance and the live model filled it with a line of the rendering, three attempts running, until the enums were injected from the contract's own constants; after that the same call validated on the first attempt. (2) The contract is strict=True, and in Pydantic's python validation mode that refuses a list where a tuple[...] is declared and an int where a float is, so every JSON array a model can emit would have been a permanent schema violation; model_validate_json keeps the strictness that is about the data and drops the one that is about Python's type vocabulary. Also measured: response_format json_schema costs 122 prompt tokens where the same schema written into a system message costs 694, so the schema belongs in the request field and not in the prompt.
makes_buildable: Task 31's triage runner has the whole model path and owes only the triage-specific parts. Call ModelClient.for_agent(settings, request.emitter), retry_policy(), and assess(request, client=..., messages=..., policy=..., propose=('classification','confidence','citations','gaps')). What 31 adds on top: the versioned prompt file with the rendering framed as data, narrowing the schema to the triage root set (helena.taxonomy's emitter_roots, which the schema does not yet enumerate), emitting the truncated gap when request.rendering.truncations is non-empty, and calling contract.check_exchange — assess deliberately does none of those. Task 32's policy engine gets an AgentResult it can constrain. D5 storage gets ModelClient.endpoint_host and Cost.retries, which are the two things concept/07 wants recorded per assessment and that no table exists for yet.

verification.detail: 1020 passed in 246.93s, full suite, engine and broker started by the fixtures. tests/test_agents.py is 39 tests: 38 against a real scripted HTTP endpoint on the loopback interface (so the transport, the headers, the JSON body and every failure mapping are exercised, not a mocked seam) and one against the CONFIGURED endpoint with the real credentials, which returned a validated AgentResult on the first attempt with no retries. `uv lock --check` clean and `python -m compileall src tests scripts` clean; no dependency was added so the lockfile is unchanged.

escalations.detail: LangChain, which concept/06-technology.md names for exactly this increment, was NOT adopted, and the decision is the operator's rather than a session's. Measured with `uv pip compile` on 2026-09-07: langchain-openai resolves to 37 distributions, and one of them is langsmith — a HARD dependency of langchain-core, not an extra. concept/06 and concept/07 both settle hosted tracing as rejected rather than deferred (a second egress channel for prompts and retrieved provider text), and tests/test_dependency_boundary.py::test_no_hosted_tracing_sdk_is_even_importable_from_the_environment asserts that `import langsmith` does not resolve anywhere in the environment. Adopting LangChain here would have meant weakening that test in the same session that introduced the thing it guards against. What was built instead is what the project already does for the feed loaders (docs/decisions/0002-dependency-set.md, helena.enrichment.fetch_public_suffix_list: 'one GET does not earn a dependency'): urllib against the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, with Pydantic — approved, and the contract's own validator — doing the structured output. The half of LangChain's justification this increment does not supply is TOOL BINDING, and it has no caller: triage binds no tools at all and the analyst's tool loop is a later increment. That increment is where the question actually has to be answered. Not blocking: the increment is complete and concept/06 itself says 'the contract is the architectural commitment and the library is a technology-table entry'.

concept/07 requires the ENDPOINT HOST to be recorded on every assessment, and the frozen agent contract has no field for it. Adding one is an escalation (concept/instruction.md §3), so it was not done. What exists instead: ModelClient.endpoint_host (host and port, with userinfo, path and query dropped rather than masked) is available to whatever stores an assessment, and every call logs it through helena.observability. That is a weaker claim than concept/07 makes, and it stays weaker until D5 builds the assessment table with an endpoint_host column. If the operator would rather it were on the contract, that is a v2 and not an edit to v1.

invariant_conflicts.documents: concept/06-technology.md's technology table (LangChain for the model client) vs concept/06 + concept/07's tracing rule (local structured logs only; a hosted tracer is a second egress channel) and concept/instruction.md §3 (a second egress channel including hosted tracing is an escalation)
invariant_conflicts.detail: Both cannot hold in this increment: langchain-core hard-depends on langsmith, so adopting the named library installs the rejected egress channel into the environment. Resolved by implementing the capability without the library and recording the conflict, per concept/instruction.md ('where a note and this file disagree, that is a defect — say so rather than picking one'). docs/decisions/0020-the-model-client.md §1 is the record.

invariant_conflicts.documents: concept/07-principles.md ('what is recorded on an assessment is the endpoint host and the model identity and version') vs the frozen helena.contracts.v1, which carries the model identity and has no endpoint field
invariant_conflicts.detail: The contract is frozen and adding a field is an escalation, so the endpoint host is exposed on the client rather than smuggled onto the contract. See the second escalation.

deferred: THE PROMPT. assess takes the messages; it does not write them. concept/04's 'the untrusted rendering clearly framed as data' and the versioned prompt file are task 31's steps by name, and writing them here would have made task 31 edit this module's text rather than add its own.

NARROWING THE SCHEMA TO THE TRIAGE ROOT SET. A classification outside the emitter's roots is already a schema violation — AgentResult raises TaxonomyError and the loop retries it — but the JSON schema does not yet ENUMERATE the permitted paths, so the model is not shown them. Given what the stance measurement showed, showing them is likely to matter; it is task 31's step and belongs with the triage prompt, and CLOSED_VOCABULARIES is the mechanism it should extend.

contract.check_exchange, AND THE TRUNCATION GAP. assess does not call it. The rule 'a rendering that truncated requires a truncated gap on the outcome' is enforced there, and the gap is a fact CODE knows rather than one the model reported — so the runner emits it and then checks the exchange. Doing it inside assess would mean this module writing a gap into a verdict it did not produce. Task 29's handover assigned it to the triage runner; that assignment stands.

AGGREGATING THE RETRY COUNT PER MODEL. concept/07 makes 'the retry count per model' a quality metric. Cost.retries is on every outcome and the structured log carries it per call with both model identities, but the metric is a query over stored assessments and no assessment table exists (task 26 deferred it to D5). So the count is typed and countable in an object, not in a row — concept/instruction.md §7's 'every new failure path is typed, stored and countable' stays open for the agent layer exactly as tasks 26-29 left it.

A TOKENIZER. The endpoint's `usage` is what is spent against the token budget. Counting tokens locally needs a tokenizer per model for a number that would be wrong for the next model — the same reasoning ADR-0019 used to bound characters rather than tokens.

A SECOND SAMPLING KNOB. temperature=0 is set for reproducibility and is not configurable. concept/07's 'budget values are policy' covers budgets; a temperature in config/agents.toml would be a knob with one value and no measurement behind it.

THE ANALYST'S TOOL LOOP. Cost.steps, live_queries and cache_hits are zero here — not because triage has no tools, which is the contract's own rule, but because this module has no tool loop at all. A non-zero count written by a module that cannot make a tool call would be a number with nothing behind it.
lessons: A PYDANTIC MODEL'S CLOSED VOCABULARIES ARE INVISIBLE TO model_json_schema(). helena.contracts.v1 enforces STANCES, GAP_KINDS, RETRIEVAL_OUTCOMES, ENTITY_TYPES and QUERY_FAILURE_REASONS in model_post_init — which is code, not a type — so the generated schema says {"type": "string"} for a field that accepts exactly two words. Measured against the live endpoint: the model filled Citation.stance with the host's rendered line, three attempts running, and the assessment became a typed failure for a vocabulary nobody had shown it. helena.agents.CLOSED_VOCABULARIES injects each one as a JSON Schema enum read from the contract's OWN constant (one copy, not two), and after that the same call validated on the first attempt. Any future increment that shows a model a schema derived from a validator-enforced class has the same hole.

VALIDATE MODEL OUTPUT WITH model_validate_json, NOT model_validate. The contract is strict=True. In Pydantic's PYTHON validation mode strict refuses a list where a tuple[...] is declared and an int where a float is; in JSON mode it accepts both, because JSON has one array type and one number type. Since every contract collection is a tuple and confidence is a float, python-mode validation would have made {"citations": [...]} and {"confidence": 1} permanent schema violations no model could ever get past — the bounded retry would have burned its whole budget on a difference between JSON and Python. JSON mode keeps every strictness that is about the data.

THE SCHEMA BELONGS IN response_format, NOT IN THE PROMPT. Measured against the configured endpoint 2026-09-07: the same triage question cost 122 prompt tokens with the schema in response_format {"type": "json_schema", "strict": true} and 694 with the same schema written into a system message — the server compiles it to a grammar rather than reading it as text. Triage is the high-volume path and pays that difference on every context. strict=true was accepted even though the schema has optional fields with defaults.

THE CONFIGURED ENDPOINT (2026-09-07): LLM_URL's path is /v1/ WITH a trailing slash, so join with rstrip('/') rather than urljoin. It supports response_format json_schema with strict true, reports usage.prompt_tokens / completion_tokens (plus prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens), and echoes the requested name in the response's `model` field — so on this endpoint today the reported model version equals the configured one. Do not turn that into an assumption: RequestVersions.completed_by exists precisely because it may stop being true.

A LIVE-ENDPOINT TEST THAT SKIPS ON FAILURE CAN PROVE NOTHING. tests/test_agents.py's live test asserts what holds for BOTH terminal outcomes first — the round trip completed, the retries stayed inside the bound, the endpoint host authenticates as nobody — and only then skips if the model produced a typed failure. A skip placed before those assertions would have turned a model regression into a green run.

THE ABSENCE OF A THING IS TESTABLE OVER THE BYTES ON THE WIRE. 'No repair-call path exists' is not a comment: a repair call has to send the model its own invalid answer back, so the property is that the discarded answer never appears in any later request, no attempt carries an `assistant` turn, and every attempt asks the same question. Same shape as 'no branch on agent identity', which is asserted by parsing src/helena/agents.py and failing if "triage" or "analyst" appears as a string constant outside a docstring.
failed_approaches: Adding langchain-openai. Not tried as an edit, resolved first: `uv pip compile` gives 37 distributions including langsmith (a hard dependency of langchain-core), openai, httpx, requests and tiktoken. langsmith's presence would fail tests/test_dependency_boundary.py::test_no_hosted_tracing_sdk_is_even_importable_from_the_environment, which exists precisely to stop a transitive tracer arriving. Do not re-derive this; it is measured, and the decision to weaken that test is the operator's.

Sending the JSON schema in a system message with response_format {"type": "json_object"}. It works and costs 694 prompt tokens against 122 for the same schema in response_format json_schema — 5.7x on the high-volume path. Rejected on the measurement.

Constructing AgentResult with keyword arguments from the parsed JSON (result_type(**proposed, emitter=..., cost=..., versions=...)). It fails on the first citation a model emits: strict python-mode validation reports 'Input should be a valid tuple' for a JSON array, which no prompt can fix. The merged dict is serialized and validated with model_validate_json instead.

Leaving the closed vocabularies out of the schema and relying on the retry loop to teach them. Tried against the live endpoint: three attempts, three different invented stance values, one typed failure. The retry loop is for errors the model can plausibly fix from the message; it is not a substitute for showing it the vocabulary.
next_session_should_know: The model path works end to end and task 31 is the triage runner on top of it. FIVE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `ModelClient.for_agent(settings, agent)`, `retry_policy()`, then `assess(request, client=..., messages=..., policy=..., propose=(...))`. `policy` has no default and `propose=None` means every proposable field — pass the triage subset ('classification', 'confidence', 'citations', 'gaps'), because the contract already refuses a triage result carrying an evidence package, a retrieval trace or a proposed claim, and offering them costs 13309 schema bytes instead of 2195 on the high-volume path. (2) YOU OWE THE TRUNCATION GAP AND check_exchange. `assess` deliberately calls neither: the gap is a fact code knows, not one the model reported, so the runner inspects `request.rendering.truncations`, emits `contract.Gap(kind=contract.TRUNCATED, ...)` and then calls `contract.check_exchange(request, outcome)`. tests/test_rendering.py::test_the_truncation_reaches_the_request_and_forces_a_gap is the worked example, including the model_copy shape. (3) SHOW THE MODEL THE ROOT SET THE WAY THE STANCES ARE SHOWN. A classification outside triage's roots already fails validation and retries, but the schema does not enumerate the permitted paths, and the measurement in this task says an unenumerated closed vocabulary is one the model invents a value for. Extend `helena.agents.CLOSED_VOCABULARIES`, or narrow `classification` in the schema from `helena.taxonomy.version(v).emitter_roots[emitter]` — a lookup, never a branch: tests/test_agents.py::test_the_module_never_names_an_agent fails if 'triage' appears as a string constant in helena/agents.py, and the same discipline is worth keeping in the runner. (4) `config/agents.toml` holds `attempts = 3` and it is a CANDIDATE, not a decision — no model's schema-violation rate has been measured because no evaluation corpus exists, and the file says what would settle it. Retries are spent against `AgentRequest.budgets.tokens`, so a run can end on the budget before it ends on the count; that outcome is `schema_invalid` with a `budget_exhausted` gap, and the two are separate on purpose. (5) THE FRAMEWORK QUESTION RETURNS WITH THE ANALYST'S TOOL LOOP AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S. docs/decisions/0020-the-model-client.md §1 has the measurement; docs/decisions/0002-dependency-set.md's 'deliberately absent' table now records it as an open escalation rather than a deadline that quietly passed. Do not adopt LangChain to get tool binding without that decision, and do not weaken test_no_hosted_tracing_sdk_is_even_importable_from_the_environment to make it fit.
